rounds.text: Meera Industries is currently trading at a significant valuation premium that is disconnected from its underlying operational performance. The stock commands a P/E ratio of 61.2x [E1], which is nearly triple the sector benchmark of 21.76x [E6], suggesting that the market has priced in aggressive growth expectations that the company is failing to meet. This disconnect is highlighted by a reverse DCF analysis, which implies the market expects 24.8% earnings growth despite the company’s base case assuming 0.0% [E42]. Furthermore, the company’s profitability metrics are consistently weak, with an ROE of 3.22% [E9] and an ROCE of 4.69% [E10], both of which fall drastically short of their respective sector benchmarks of 11.24% and 12.9% [E9, E10]. Compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months has plummeted by 61% [E19], and the long-term trend shows a 15% decline in compounded profit growth over five years [E17]. Conceded: the company maintains a healthy dividend payout of 41.1% [E46] and has successfully reduced its working capital requirements from 69.7 days to 42.9 days [E47]. Ultimately, the combination of a -517.3% margin of safety [E41] and a declining promoter stake [E38] indicates that the current share price is unsupported by the firm's actual delivery.
